bare-plateau.name: Bare plateau
bare-plateau.ground: bare pale basalt benches with hexagonal-jointed tops, scree fans, thin wind-scoured grass only in cracks; no meadow
bare-plateau.rock: pale warm basalt, stepped benches and low column walls, talus at every foot
bare-plateau.trees: none on the open plateau; a few dark conifers in gullies
bare-plateau.water: tarns lying in bare rock; thin tall falls off the bench edges
bare-plateau.palette: pale warm greys and creams, cool teal water, sparse grey-green

moor.name: Heather moor
moor.ground: open heather-and-grass moor, wind-scoured, boulders and scrub; heather sparse and subdued, never a carpet
moor.rock: low basalt outcrops and boulder fields, an occasional column wall
moor.trees: dark conifers only in gullies and hollows
moor.water: becks in shallow gullies, small pools
moor.palette: olive and gold-green, dull violet accents, grey rock

dark-forest.name: Dark forest gorge
dark-forest.ground: dense dark conifer stands on mossy ground, little open ground, flat haze in the gorge
dark-forest.rock: mossy basalt gorge walls, wet talus
dark-forest.trees: dense dark conifers, the darkest green in the territory
dark-forest.water: a gorge stream with falls, pools in shade
dark-forest.palette: deep greens, near-black under the stands, grey-blue haze

coast-cliff.name: Wild coast
coast-cliff.ground: bare basalt benches and talus above sea-cliffs, thin grass, shingle coves; no meadow
coast-cliff.rock: tall columnar sea-cliffs, WEATHERED and irregular: columns of uneven height and width, tops broken at different levels, split and leaning columns, collapsed drums lying in talus at the foot, lichen in the joints; the cliff line wanders in plan with bays and buttresses, never a straight run or a square corner, never a regular palisade of identical cylinders (this is ordinary coast, where regularity would be an accident — the linked-colonnade biome is the deliberate exception and says so); a natural ledge partway up the face; sea stacks offshore
coast-cliff.water: the sea on the seaward edge with surf and wash; an occasional tarn on a shelf
coast-cliff.palette: pale grey rock, teal to deep-blue sea, sparse green

sound-coast.name: Sound coast
sound-coast.ground: bare rock diving into the sound, shingle, thin grass
sound-coast.rock: low basalt slabs and ledges running on under the water
sound-coast.water: the sound (sea) on the seaward edge, clear shallows over slabs
sound-coast.palette: grey slabs, turquoise shallows to deep teal

quarry.name: Construction quarry
quarry.ground: cut benches, quarried faces, spoil fans, a levelled floor; works read from landform only
quarry.rock: fresh pale cut rock and column walls
quarry.trees: a few dark conifers on the rim and in the drainage gully
quarry.water: a flooded pit, the drainage stream, the sea where coastal
quarry.palette: pale cut rock, dust, a thin green rim

mixed-bench.name: Bench country
mixed-bench.ground: stepped benches and terraces, scree, moor on the flats
mixed-bench.trees: conifer stands on the sheltered benches

lush-shelf.name: Settlement shelf
lush-shelf.ground: the richest ground in its neighbourhood: meadow green warmed with gold, glades, flowers allowed here
lush-shelf.rock: low outcrops and natural terraces that a settlement could sit on
lush-shelf.trees: orchard-like conifer stands with open glades
lush-shelf.water: a stream through the shelf, a pool

magical-gorge.name: Magical gorge (moment)
magical-gorge.ground: a deep gorge with flat mist; the ground around it is moor
magical-gorge.rock: column walls; rock fragments floating above the gorge trailing roots and moss
magical-gorge.water: a great fall into faintly glowing water
magical-gorge.palette: moor palette plus violet crystal glow and luminous teal
magical-gorge.wonders: floating rock fragments with crystals; self-luminous crystal outcrops that cast no light; faintly glowing water at the fall

purple-field.name: The purple field (unique)
purple-field.ground: a saturated magenta-violet carpet of grass and low bloom on magenta soil filling the whole cell; tufts of pale lavender-blue grass; clumps of gold, orange, red and pale-blue flowering shrubs
purple-field.rock: a crystal-crowned knoll rising from the field; low outcrops
purple-field.trees: pink-blossom broadleaf trees standing in the field; dark conifers only at the edges
purple-field.palette: saturated magenta-violet ground, high-key and bright, purple as the base and the other hues as accents

linked-colonnade.name: The linked colonnade (unique)
linked-colonnade.ground: a narrow cliff-top bench of thin grass and bare rock running the length of the cell, deliberately plain and quiet: the colonnade is the only event here and nothing else competes with it
linked-colonnade.rock: THE ONE PLACE IN THIS WORLD WITH DELIBERATE ORDER, and it must be drawn as order — the geology rule's ban on a regular palisade governs regularity that arrives by accident, and this is asked for. Basalt columns that ALL LEAN THE SAME WAY, each touching the next at the top, joined into one unbroken arcade that runs the whole length of the cliff, leaves the land at the shore and continues as a line of linked sea stacks out past the edge of the authored world. Caught mid-topple, as though a single wave passed through the rock and stayed. Every column the same height and girth as its neighbours: none larger, none singled out, NOTHING STANDING AT THE MIDDLE — the chain has no centre and that must be visible. You can walk under the arcade. Do not weather this back into an irregular cliff; the ordinary cliffs elsewhere are what make it read
linked-colonnade.trees: none on the bench; a few dark conifers in the gullies behind it
linked-colonnade.water: the sea below the arcade, surf breaking between the stacks and through the arches
linked-colonnade.palette: pale warm basalt against deep teal sea; the arcade reads by the gaps between its columns, not by shading
linked-colonnade.wonders: the colonnade itself — an unbroken chain of equal columns, each joined only to the next, all leaning one way, running on past the horizon

rules.geology: columnar basalt, bedded and jointed, talus at cliff bases; plateau-and-gorge — columns are a feature where the biome says so, not the ground everywhere. Columns are WEATHERED and irregular wherever they appear: uneven heights and widths, broken tops, split and leaning columns, collapsed drums in talus, lichen in the joints; never a regular palisade of identical cylinders, never a square corner (owner, 2026-09-01: 'the cliff side is unnatural'). THAT BAN IS ON REGULARITY THAT ARRIVES BY DEFAULT, NOT ON ORDER THAT IS ASKED FOR (owner, 2026-09-03: 'thats only true if unintentional'). Where a biome or a site explicitly calls for regular, ordered or repeating columns, that order is the whole point: draw it exactly as specified and do not weather it back into an irregular cliff. The rule above governs everything that was not asked for, which is almost all of the world — that is what makes the exceptions read as wonders.
rules.vegetation: conifer in gullies and shelter, thinning on exposed rock; scrub and heather on open ground; crowns 4-7 m; the biome sets the mix
rules.water: coastal cliff and shingle seaward; inland tarns on shelves draining by falls into gorges
rules.buildable: ~1/3 occupiable shelf, separated by gorges and broken ground so settlements read distinct
rules.rail: fantasy railway: tunnels, improbable spans and submerged runs permitted; land supplies the drama, not the gradient. The north-east leg spans the bay NinjaOne's ruling puts at that corner, so that coast must open into water wide enough for the line to leap it.
rules.lighting: flat: every rock face the same value whichever way it faces; ambient occlusion only; no directional key, no lit side, no cast shadows
rules.northBorder: OWNER RULING 2026-09-01, read from NinjaOne's side and mapped onto this block (NinjaOne is at lattice [3,1], this block at [2,5], so local col L is world col 2+L): NinjaOne and Tanium share BOTH a land and an ocean border — a SOUND to the west, solid connecting LAND in the middle, a BAY to the east, so the two territories are one island with a waist. Local cells 1,0 and 2,0 (world cols 3 and 4): the north edge opens into the SOUND, the same water NinjaOne's 0,3 and 1,3 open into, and the inlet crossing and submerged run live on the far side of it. Local cells 3,0 and 4,0 (world cols 5 and 6): the north edge is LAND continuing into NinjaOne — terrain must run to the north edge as solid connecting ground, no coast. Local cell 5,0 (world col 7): the north-east bay, sea as authored. Local cells 0,0 and 6,0 (world cols 2 and 8) have no NinjaOne above them: open sea to the north. MEASURED HANDOVER, from the authored NinjaOne art on the shared line rather than from the cell granularity of the ruling above — the art is more generous with land than the ruling, and this is what actually arrives: the sound's south shore ENDS at world col 4.38, land runs unbroken from world col 4.38 to 7.34 (283 m), and the bay's shore BEGINS at world col 7.34. Two becks cross that ground and must be met on this side: one 1.9 m wide at world col 5.30, one 3.8 m at world col 6.55. So local cell 2,0 is sound on its western 38% and land on its eastern 62%, and local cell 5,0 is land on its western 34% and bay beyond.
